newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CiU says health talks at advanced stage.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CiU says health talks at advanced stage.

text.p: Spanish government ally Catalan Convergencia i Unio (CiU) said on Thursday that talks with the government on increasing health spending for the 1998 budget are at an advanced stage.
"Health, to which we give a lot of importance, is at a very advanced stage," CiU economic spokesman Francesc Homs told Reuters in an interview.

He said the committee studying the issue already recognised that expenditures for health financing would rise by 200 billion pesetas in 1998, which will be covered by an expected increase in revenues.
The government also projects additional spending of 100/120 billion pesetas for which it must find alternative ways of financing.
He did not rule out the possibility reported recently by the Spanish press of raising special taxes, such as the ones on alcohol and tobacco.
"This may take place but it will not necessarily take place," he said. "We are awaiting the government's final decision on this."
The ruling minority Popular Party government needs the CiU's legislative votes to pass the budget. The CiU backs the PP in an alliance but is not part of the government.
